title: Addis Ababa – Cultural Discovery Tour
tagline: The diplomatic and cultural capital where ancient heritage meets modern African dynamism.
overview: Discover the vibrant pulse of Addis Ababa, Africa’s diplomatic capital nestled in the Entoto eucalyptus highlands at 2,350 meters. From the fossil of humankind's ancestor 'Lucy' at the National Museum to the panoramic vistas of Mount Entoto and the aromatic stalls of the world-famous Mercato, this immersive city discovery reveals the historic roots and living culture of Ethiopia.
communityImpactFocus: Supports local Addis cultural heritage guides, traditional handicraft cooperatives, and authentic community dining.
highlights: National Museum of Ethiopia & 3.2-million-year-old hominid Lucy (Dinknesh)
Holy Trinity Cathedral with imperial tombs of Emperor Haile Selassie
Panoramic views of the capital from Mount Entoto at 3,200m
Traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony with freshly roasted wild beans
Addis Mercato, Africa's largest vibrant open-air marketplace
included: Airport transfers and private air-conditioned vehicle transport
Professional licensed English-speaking local tour guide
All entrance fees to museums, cathedrals, and historical viewpoints
Authentic traditional coffee ceremony experience
1 night hotel accommodation in 4-star central Addis hotel
Breakfast and welcome cultural dinner with traditional music and dance
Purified bottled water throughout the tour
notIncluded: Tips and gratuities for guides and drivers

itinerary.title: Welcome to Addis Ababa – Imperial History & Lucy
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Bole International Airport, meet your Yared Tour representative and transfer to your hotel. Begin your exploration at the National Museum, home to Lucy (Dinknesh) and ancient Aksumite artifacts. Continue to the majestic Holy Trinity Cathedral, resting place of Emperor Haile Selassie, followed by an authentic Ethiopian coffee ceremony in a serene heritage courtyard.
itinerary.overnight: Addis Ababa (Jupiter International or Radisson Blu)

itinerary.title: Mount Entoto Panoramic Heights & Addis Mercato
itinerary.description: Ascend the lush eucalyptus-covered hills to Mount Entoto (3,200m) to visit Emperor Menelik II's historic palace and St. Mary church with stunning panoramic views over the sprawling capital. In the afternoon, explore the lively rhythms of Mercato, navigating spice lanes, hand-woven cotton textiles, and recycled metalwork with our expert guide.

title: Hawassa, Sidama & Yirgacheffe Coffee Lands
tagline: Gentle lakes, rich birdlife, and the birthplace of world-renowned specialty coffee.
overview: Journey south through the Great Rift Valley to the shores of Lake Hawassa and the lush emerald hills of Sidama and Yirgacheffe. Experience the morning bustle of Hawassa's iconic fish market, watch marabou storks and colobus monkeys in lakeside fig trees, and walk through shade-grown coffee farms meeting smallholder producers who harvest some of the finest Arabica beans on earth.
communityImpactFocus: Direct partnerships with Sidama smallholder coffee farmers and Lake Hawassa artisanal fishing associations.
highlights: Bustling morning fish market at Lake Hawassa with fresh tilapia
Boat excursion to observe hippos, white pelicans, and kingfishers
Walk among wild coffee trees in family-run organic farms of Sidama
Tasting single-origin freshly washed Yirgacheffe coffees
Enset (false banana) culinary demonstrations in local Sidama bamboo homesteads
included: Private 4WD Land Cruiser transport with experienced driver
English-speaking professional guide & local coffee community specialists
Lake Hawassa private boat tour
Coffee plantation tour & community cupping session
2 nights accommodation in lakeside resort / eco-lodge
All meals (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner) and mineral water
All regional road taxes and entrance fees
notIncluded: Personal purchases of specialty roasted coffee

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa to Lake Hawassa via the Great Rift Valley
itinerary.description: Depart Addis Ababa driving south through the Great Rift Valley, passing crater lakes Ziway and Langano. Arrive in the scenic city of Hawassa along the lake shore. Take a peaceful afternoon stroll along the promenade where black-and-white colobus monkeys play among giant fig trees.

itinerary.title: Hawassa Fish Market & Sidama Coffee Immersion
itinerary.description: Rise early to visit the vibrant Lake Hawassa fish market as fishermen dock wooden canoes laden with fresh catch, surrounded by flocks of marabou storks. Continue into the lush green hills of Sidama to visit community coffee plots under forest canopies. Witness the harvest and wet-mill processing, followed by a warm lunch in a traditional bamboo Sidama home.

itinerary.title: Lake Hawassa Boat Safari & Return to Addis
itinerary.description: Embark on a relaxing boat trip across Lake Hawassa to spot resident hippo pods and abundant waterbirds. After lunch with views across the lake, return comfortably to Addis Ababa with stops at Rift Valley roadside fruit markets.

title: Arba Minch & Gamo Highlands
tagline: Two glistening rift valley lakes, giant crocodiles, and the unique beehive bamboo homes of the Dorze people.
overview: Set between the shimmering waters of Lake Chamo and Lake Abaya, Arba Minch ('Forty Springs') is southern Ethiopia’s natural crossroads. Venture by boat across Lake Chamo to witness the famed 'crocodile market' where giant Nile crocodiles bask beside hippos, then climb into the mist-shrouded Gamo Highlands to discover the Dorze people, famed for their towering beehive bamboo architecture and extraordinary cotton weaving.
communityImpactFocus: Supports the Dorze community weaving collective and sustainable community village lodge initiatives.
highlights: Lake Chamo boat safari to observe Africa's largest Nile crocodiles and hippos
Traditional bamboo architecture tour in Chencha Dorze village
Hands-on demonstration of making bread from false banana (Kocho)
Traditional polyphonic singing and vibrant bamboo loom weaving
Spectacular cliff-edge sunset over lakes Abaya and Chamo at Nechisar
included: Domestic flight Addis Ababa - Arba Minch (or private 4WD ground transport)
Private boat excursion on Lake Chamo
All park fees, local community village dues, and scout costs
Dorze community cultural workshop and musical exchange
2 nights lodging (Paradise Lodge Arba Minch or Dorze Community Lodge)
All meals and purified drinking water
Professional bilingual guide

itinerary.title: Arrival in Arba Minch & Forty Springs Walk
itinerary.description: Fly from Addis Ababa to Arba Minch or drive via the scenic Rift Valley. Check into your lodge perched high above the 'Bridge of God' ridge dividing Lake Abaya and Lake Chamo. Take a refreshing nature walk through the lush groundwater forest to see the forty crystal-clear natural springs that give the town its name.
itinerary.overnight: Arba Minch (Paradise Lodge or Haile Resort)

itinerary.title: Lake Chamo Boat Safari & Nechisar Wildlife
itinerary.description: Board a private boat on Lake Chamo to reach the legendary 'Crocodile Market'—a sandbank where colossal Nile crocodiles congregate alongside pods of snorting hippopotamuses and vibrant goliath herons. In the afternoon, explore the plains of Nechisar to spot Burchell's zebras and gazelles.

itinerary.title: Chencha Dorze Village & Gamo Highlands Immersion
itinerary.description: Climb up the winding mountain pass to Chencha in the Gamo Highlands (2,600m). Meet the friendly Dorze people whose towering bamboo houses resemble elephant heads and last up to 80 years. Learn how they scrape false banana roots to ferment dough, bake fresh Kocho with local honey, and weave intricate textiles on wooden foot looms before returning to the airport.

title: Omo Valley Discovery Journey
tagline: A respectful, ethical journey through Africa's most culturally distinct river valley.
overview: The Lower Omo Valley is a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape home to ancient pastoralist and agro-pastoralist communities. Traveling with Yared's certified local guides, this journey emphasizes cultural dignity, meaningful dialogue, and fair economic exchange with the Hamer, Mursi, Karo, and Dassanech peoples, moving away from exploitative tourism toward authentic human-to-human connection.
communityImpactFocus: Direct village elder compensation, fair photography fees pooled for community health/schools, and local native guides.
highlights: Meaningful village visits with the Hamer, Mursi, Karo, and Konso peoples
Konso UNESCO terraced agriculture and stone-walled village compounds
Mago National Park excursion to the secluded Mursi settlements
Karo clifftop village overlooking the dramatic curves of the Omo River
Authentic weekly tribal market day at Key Afer or Dimeka
included: 4WD Land Cruiser with experienced expedition driver and all fuel
Yared cultural tour director plus local tribal guides and community scouts
All regional community entrance fees and ethical village compensation
4 nights accommodation in best available eco-lodges / safari tents
Full board (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner) and continuous purified water
Konso Cultural Heritage Site guided excursion
notIncluded: Personal camera permit fees for specific portraits where requested
Gratuities for drivers and local scouts

itinerary.title: Arba Minch to Konso UNESCO Landscape & Key Afer
itinerary.description: Drive south to the terraced hills of Konso, celebrated for 400-year-old stone terraces and wooden ancestral waga carvings. Continue to Key Afer or Turmi, taking in the vibrant pastoralist atmosphere of southern Ethiopia.

itinerary.title: Mago National Park & Respectful Mursi Visit
itinerary.description: Drive into Mago National Park to visit a remote Mursi village. Famous for their clay lip plates and body art, our visit is conducted with deep cultural awareness and unhurried conversation led by local guides who speak the Mursi language.

itinerary.title: Karo People & Omo River Panorama
itinerary.description: Travel across savanna plains to the clifftop settlement of Kolcho, home to the Karo community. Enjoy sweeping views over the winding Omo River and learn about intricate chalk body painting traditions and fishing customs.

itinerary.title: Dassanech at Omorate & Hamer Village Life
itinerary.description: Cross the Omo River in traditional dugout canoes to visit the Dassanech semi-nomadic pastoralists. In the late afternoon, return to Turmi to walk through a peaceful Hamer family compound, learning about cattle culture and beekeeping.

itinerary.title: Turmi Market & Return via Arba Minch
itinerary.description: Catch the lively morning exchanges at the local market where different communities gather to trade livestock, gourds, and honey. Transfer comfortably to Jinka Airport for your flight back to Addis Ababa.

title: South Omo – Soshi Trekking
tagline: Walk the trails of tradition – an immersion into the Omo Valley’s living cultures on foot.
overview: The Soshi Trekking Route was developed by Yared Tour & Travel in direct partnership with local Ari communities. Bypassing standard road vehicle tourism, this trek travels along age-old walking trails between quiet mountain hamlets, terraced fields, and forested river gorges. Experience true hospitality as village families welcome you into their daily rhythm.
communityImpactFocus: 100% community-managed route: local village hosts, community porters, and trail maintenance fund.
highlights: Trek scenic mountain footpaths between secluded Ari and Banna villages
Homestay accommodations in community guest compounds
Traditional pottery, blacksmithing, and honey extraction demonstrations
Wildcard wildlife spotting: baboons, bushbuck, and endemic songbirds
Evening campfire gatherings with village elders sharing oral histories
included: All trail guiding by licensed Ari local mountain guides and scouts
Luggage transport with pack mules or porters
3 nights accommodation (community eco-camps and village homestays)
All meals freshly prepared using organic local highland produce
Purified drinking water and snacks on trail
All community fees, village hosting dues, and camera permits
notIncluded: Personal trekking gear (sleeping bag, boots, headlamp)
Alcoholic drinks and tips for muleteers

itinerary.title: Jinka to Soshi Highland Trailhead
itinerary.description: Meet your trekking crew in Jinka and drive to the mountain trailhead. Begin walking along lush green ridges through bamboo groves and coffee groves into the Soshi highlands. Arrive at our first village camp and enjoy a warm communal meal prepared with farm-fresh vegetables.

itinerary.title: Deep Highland Valley Trek & Artisan Encounters
itinerary.description: Hike through rolling river valleys and terraced farmlands. Stop at family workshops where women mold clay pots by hand and blacksmiths forge farming tools over charcoal bellows. Continue over gentle passes with expansive views.

itinerary.title: Trek through Sacred Forests & River Cascades
itinerary.description: Follow mountain trails down towards shaded river ravines where natural waterfalls provide refreshing swimming spots. Learn about indigenous medicinal plants and forest honey gathering from our community guides.

itinerary.title: Descent to Trail End & Farewell to Ari Hosts
itinerary.description: Complete the final scenic descent of the trekking circuit. Meet our support vehicle for a farewell toast with fresh local coffee and transfer back to Jinka for a hot shower and evening relaxation.

title: Ari Zone – Weset Trekking
tagline: Trek through mountains, hidden waterfalls, and lush agricultural forests with the Ari people.
overview: The Ari people are the largest ethnic community of South Omo, renowned for their fertile green highlands, painted clay huts, and welcoming spirit. Starting from Jinka, this 4-day community trek winds through mist-clad volcanic hills, cascading mountain streams, and self-sufficient farming villages where life moves to the rhythm of the seasons.
communityImpactFocus: Pioneered by Yared Tour to channel tourism revenue directly to Ari village councils and women's cooperatives.
highlights: Hike along quiet forest ridges and sparkling mountain waterfalls
Authentic stay in traditionally painted Ari compound huts
Participate in daily farming, cardamom harvest, and honey harvesting
Traditional pottery craft and injera-baking workshops
Clean mountain air and unspoiled natural tranquility
included: Expert local Ari trekking guide and village coordinators
All trail meals, drinking water, and field cook services
3 nights community camp/homestay accommodation
Luggage transport via pack mules
Village conservation fees and photography contributions
notIncluded: Trekking sleeping bag and personal clothing

itinerary.title: Hike from Jinka to Upper Ari Villages
itinerary.description: Leave Jinka behind and ascend steadily into the fertile Ari hills. Admire neat compounds decorated with intricate mud patterns and bright flower gardens. Arrive at our community base in time for sundown.

itinerary.title: Weset Waterfall Trail & River Gorge
itinerary.description: Trek through indigenous tree canopies where colobus monkeys reside. Descend to the spectacular Weset waterfall for a picnic lunch beside the cool spray. Continue across gentle rolling farmland.

itinerary.title: Agricultural Life & Traditional Ari Distillery
itinerary.description: Spend the morning with local farmers learning about crop rotations, enset cultivation, and traditional small-batch distillation of areki. Enjoy an afternoon hike over panoramic mountain ridges.

itinerary.title: Scenic Loop Return to Jinka
itinerary.description: Walk the final stretch of trail overlooking the vast plains of the lower Omo Valley in the distance. Arrive in Jinka for lunch and celebration of a successful trekking expedition.

title: Borena – Camel Hiking & Cultural Encounters
tagline: Walk the rhythm of the savanna – where singing wells, camels, and ancient traditions tell the story of Borena life.
overview: Journey to Ethiopia’s southern borderlands to the arid thorn savannas of Borena. Here, one of Africa’s oldest democratic governance systems—the Gadaa system—thrives alongside resilient pastoralist traditions. Trek alongside camel caravans across ancient volcanic craters, and witness the mesmerizing spectacle of the singing wells, where chains of men sing in rhythm as they haul water for thousands of cattle.
communityImpactFocus: Direct support for Borena pastoral water conservation projects and local camel handler associations.
highlights: The world-famous 'Singing Wells' (Tula Wells) of the Borena pastoralists
Trek across the dramatic caldera rim of El Sod (the 'House of Salt')
Witness salt miners diving into the jet-black subterranean volcanic lake
Learn about the ancient UNESCO-inscribed Gadaa democratic social system
Trek through acacia savannas with camel caravans carrying supplies
included: Private 4WD expedition vehicle with driver and fuel
Experienced Borena cultural guide and community scouts
Camel caravan support for day hikes across savanna trails
3 nights lodging (Yabello Motel / Yabello Eco-camp)
All meals and purified mineral water
All local community permissions, well entrance fees, and salt lake dues
notIncluded: Gratuities for camel handlers and well singers

itinerary.title: Journey South into Borena Acacia Savannas
itinerary.description: Drive south through picturesque landscape transitions from lush green hills to sprawling acacia savannas. Spot roadside camel herds and distinctive Borena settlements fenced with acacia thorns. Arrive in Yabello by late afternoon.

itinerary.title: The Singing Wells of Dublock
itinerary.description: Visit the subterranean Singing Wells at Dublock. Up to ten men stand on wooden ledges down a deep hand-dug shaft, passing buckets hand-over-hand while singing hypnotic rhythmic chants that soothe the cattle waiting patiently in long lines above.

itinerary.title: El Sod Salt Crater Hike with Camel Caravan
itinerary.description: Drive to the giant extinct volcano crater of El Sod. Hike down the steep, dramatic path accompanied by camels to the obsidian-black salt lake at the crater floor. Watch brave local salt harvesters diving into sulfurous mineral water to scoop out precious black salt.

itinerary.title: Borena Cultural Council & Return Journey
itinerary.description: Meet with community elders to gain insight into the democratic Gadaa generational leadership system. Begin your comfortable return journey northwards through the Rift Valley.

title: Jimma & Bonga – The Story of Coffee, Tea, Honey & Spices
tagline: Follow the wild origins of Arabica coffee deep into the cloud forests of Kaffa.
overview: Journey into the lush, mountainous southwest of Ethiopia to the ancient kingdom of Kaffa—the historic birthplace of wild Coffea arabica. Walk through virgin cloud forests where coffee bushes grow wild beneath giant mahogany trees draped in orchids and lianas. Explore King Abba Jifar’s 19th-century palace in Jimma, breathe in terraced tea plantations, and sample pure white forest honey directly from tree hives.
communityImpactFocus: Supports the Kaffa UNESCO Biosphere Reserve conservation team and wild forest honey cooperatives.
highlights: Hike into the wild ancestral coffee forests of the Kaffa Biosphere Reserve
Traditional forest coffee brewing ritual with roasted coriander and rue
Visit Emperor Abba Jifar's wooden royal palace in Jimma
Taste organic white forest honey and wild spices (korarima, timiz)
Bonga natural hot springs and forest waterfalls
included: Private 4WD Land Cruiser transport with driver and fuel
Specialist botanical and cultural forest guides
3 nights accommodation in Jimma & Bonga eco-lodges
All meals and bottled water
Forest biosphere permits and palace entrance tickets
Coffee cupping and spice cooperative workshop
notIncluded: Domestic flight Jimma - Addis (if chosen over driving)

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa to Jimma via Gibe River Valley
itinerary.description: Drive west across fertile Oromo plateau farmlands and descend into the scenic Gibe River gorge. Arrive in Jimma, the historical capital of the Kingdom of Jimma. Tour the 1880s palace of King Abba Jifar, crafted from indigenous hardwoods with intricate Arabesque woodwork.

itinerary.title: Jimma to Bonga & Kaffa UNESCO Biosphere
itinerary.description: Drive deeper into the moist evergreen rainforest to Bonga, center of the Kaffa UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Walk through the Mankira forest where the legend of Kaldi and his dancing goats first discovered coffee. Witness wild coffee trees growing naturally in the dense understory.

itinerary.title: Bonga Waterfalls, Hot Springs & Forest Honey
itinerary.description: Hike to the roaring Barta Waterfall through bamboo forests. Meet wild honey harvesters who climb 30-meter trees to place woven bamboo hives, and taste fragrant white honey straight from the comb. Relax at the natural mineral hot springs.

itinerary.title: Wushwush Tea Estate & Return Journey
itinerary.description: Visit the emerald green carpets of the Wushwush Tea Estate, Ethiopia's largest tea plantation. Transfer to Jimma Airport for a short 45-minute flight to Addis Ababa, or drive back enjoying picturesque western highland vistas.

title: Bale Mountains & Harenna Forest
tagline: Ethiopia’s wild heart – where the endangered Ethiopian wolf still roams free across alpine plateaus.
overview: Bale Mountains National Park is one of the world's premier biodiversity hotspots, conserving the largest continuous afro-alpine plateau on the African continent. Ascend to the windswept Sanetti Plateau at over 4,000 meters to spot the world's rarest canid—the endangered Ethiopian wolf—hunting giant mole-rats. Then drop dramatically off the southern escarpment into the mysterious moss-draped cloud canopy of the ancient Harenna Forest.
communityImpactFocus: Direct partnership with local Bale community scouts and forest conservation horse-trekking guides.
highlights: Spotting the critically endangered Ethiopian Wolf on the high Sanetti Plateau
Drive Africa's highest all-weather road past Mount Tullu Dimtu (4,377m)
Explore the moss-carpeted, primordial Harenna Cloud Forest
Observe endemic Mountain Nyala, Menelik's bushbuck, and Bale monkeys
Pristine alpine tarns, giant lobelia forests, and spectacular birdlife
included: Expedition 4WD Land Cruiser equipped for mountain terrain
Licensed national park naturalist guide and armed local wildlife scout
2 nights accommodation (Bale Mountain Lodge or Tokuma Goba)
All park entry, vehicle fees, and community scout dues
Full board meals and pure mountain bottled water

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa to Dinsho Headquarters
itinerary.description: Drive southeast through the fertile Arsi agricultural plains towards the Bale Mountains. Arrive at Dinsho, national park headquarters. Take an afternoon woodland hike through juniper and Hagenia forests to spot the majestic Mountain Nyala, Menelik’s bushbuck, and warthogs grazing freely.

itinerary.title: Sanetti Afro-Alpine Plateau & Ethiopian Wolf Safari
itinerary.description: Ascend to the breathtaking Sanetti Plateau (4,000m+), a surreal lunar-like landscape studded with towering giant lobelias. Keep binoculars ready: this is the premier habitat of the Ethiopian wolf. Ascend Tullu Dimtu (4,377m), then descend the dramatic Harenna escarpment into lush bamboo and cloud forests in search of the endemic Bale monkey.

itinerary.title: Sof Omar Caves or Rift Valley Lakes Return
itinerary.description: Enjoy a final morning wildlife drive before returning towards Addis Ababa, or take an optional extension to the colossal limestone caverns of Sof Omar, carved by the Web River.

title: Danakil Depression – The Hottest Place on Earth
tagline: Where fire, salt, and spirit meet – an otherworldly expedition into volcanic wonders.
overview: Dropping to 125 meters below sea level, the Danakil Depression in the Afar triangle is one of the most geologically raw and dramatic landscapes on the planet. Trek at night to the glowing lava lake rim of the active Erta Ale shield volcano, marvel at the neon-yellow acid hot springs of Dallol, and watch Afar camel caravans cutting salt blocks on endless shimmering salt flats.
communityImpactFocus: Employment of native Afar guides, camel drivers, and local safety escorts, ensuring tourism directly enriches Afar families.
highlights: Night trek to the crater rim of active Erta Ale volcano and its boiling lava lake
The psychedelic mineral terraces and sulfur chimneys of Dallol hydrothermal field
Lake Karum salt mining where Afar miners carve and pack salt onto camel trains
Swimming in the hyper-saline waters of Lake Afrera
Sleeping under a blanket of desert stars on traditional woven wooden beds
included: Full convoy of modern air-conditioned 4WD Toyota Land Cruisers
Professional Yared expedition leader, Afar tribal scouts, and police escorts
All meals cooked fresh by dedicated expedition camp chef
3 nights accommodation (open-air traditional Afar desert camp & Semera hotel)
Mattresses, fresh linens, sleeping bags, and camping equipment
Abundant chilled bottled water, juices, and snacks throughout
All regional Afar administration road permits and crater fees
notIncluded: Tips for expedition crew and local Afar scouts

itinerary.title: Semera to Lake Afrera & Salt Springs
itinerary.description: Meet in Semera, capital of the Afar region, and drive across black lava fields toward Lake Afrera (102m below sea level). Float effortlessly in the hypersaline lake and soothe tired muscles in natural freshwater hot springs as the sunset reflects off the water.

itinerary.title: Erta Ale Active Volcano Night Trek
itinerary.description: Drive across sandy desert tracks to Dodom camp at the base of Erta Ale. Rest during the midday heat. At sunset, begin the exhilarating 3-4 hour trek up the gentle slope of the volcano to the caldera rim. Stand in awe watching glowing red magma churn inside the active lava lake beneath the night sky.
itinerary.overnight: Erta Ale Caldera Rim Camp (Open-air traditional beds)

itinerary.title: Erta Ale Sunrise to Dallol & Hamed Ela
itinerary.description: Watch sunrise over the volcanic crater before descending back to base camp for breakfast. Drive across ancient salt basins to Hamed Ela, a traditional salt caravan outpost. Enjoy sunset drinks over the vast mirror-like salt flats of Lake Karum.

itinerary.title: Dallol Hydrothermal Wonders & Salt Mines to Semera
itinerary.description: Visit Dallol, the lowest land volcano on earth (-125m), marveling at surreal neon-green, sulfur-yellow, and rust-red mineral chimneys and bubbling acid pools. Visit nearby salt canyon pillars and traditional Afar salt cutters before returning to Semera.

title: Harar – The Holy Walled City
tagline: History, faith, and living traditions within centuries-old labyrinthine defensive walls.
overview: Harar Jugol is a UNESCO World Heritage site and the spiritual heart of Islamic Ethiopia, revered as the fourth holiest city of Islam. Enclosed within 16th-century fortress walls lie 368 winding alleyways, 82 mosques, vibrant spice markets, and distinctive traditional Adare townhouse architecture. Experience the legendary nightly ritual where the 'Hyena Men' of Harar call wild spotted hyenas by name and feed them meat by hand.
communityImpactFocus: Direct partnerships with Harari family cultural guesthouses and local heritage preservation guides.
highlights: Witnessing the ancient nightly wild hyena feeding ritual outside the historic city walls
Wandering the colorful, narrow pedestrian alleys of UNESCO-listed Harar Jugol
Touring a traditional Harari Adare cultural home with hand-woven basketry
Exploring French poet Arthur Rimbaud's historic wooden mansion and museum
Sampling famous Harar coffee and aromatic spice markets
included: Airport transfers between Dire Dawa and Harar
Private vehicle transport and fuel
Licensed English-speaking Harari heritage guide
2 nights lodging in traditional heritage guesthouse or hotel
All entrance fees to museums, Rimbaud house, and hyena feeding site
All meals and bottled drinking water

itinerary.title: Dire Dawa to Harar & The Nightly Hyena Ceremony
itinerary.description: Fly into Dire Dawa and drive up the rocky escarpment to walled Harar. Settle into a traditional Harari cultural guesthouse. At dusk, gather outside the city gate to witness the remarkable 'Hyena Man' summon wild hyenas from the darkness, feeding them strips of meat directly from his hands and mouth.
itinerary.overnight: Harar (Rowda Cultural Guest House or Ras Hotel)

itinerary.title: Ancient Jugol Alleys, Mosques & Rimbaud House
itinerary.description: Spend the full day exploring inside the walls of Jugol. Visit the Grand Jami Mosque, the vibrant Shoa Gate market, and the Arthur Rimbaud Museum with its stained-glass windows. Visit an authentic Adare family home decorated with ceremonial niches and woven agergada baskets.

itinerary.title: Koremi Clifftop Village & Dire Dawa Railway Heritage
itinerary.description: Visit the stone cliff village of Koremi, perched dramatically over khat and coffee valleys. Return to Dire Dawa to explore the historic French-built Franco-Ethiopian railway station and colonial quarter before your return flight to Addis Ababa.

title: Grand Ethiopia Journey – Bale, Harar, Jimma & Arba Minch
tagline: From mountains to markets, coffee forests to desert dreams – discover Ethiopia's soul in one grand journey.
overview: The ultimate comprehensive exploration of Ethiopia's diverse geography, wildlife, and cultural tapestries. Connecting the alpine heights of Bale Mountains where the rare Ethiopian wolf thrives, the medieval Islamic walled citadel of Harar, the virgin coffee biospheres of Kaffa and Jimma, and the vibrant rift lakes and indigenous cultures of Arba Minch, this signature 12-day route weaves together the extraordinary contrast and authentic soul of Ethiopia.
communityImpactFocus: Comprehensive sustainable travel supporting community guides and conservation cooperatives across five distinct regions.
highlights: Complete combination of mountains, lakes, historical citadels, and wild coffee forests
Ethiopian wolf tracking across the 4,000m Sanetti Plateau in Bale Mountains
Nightly hyena feeding ritual and UNESCO walled city exploration in Harar
Lake Chamo crocodile boat safari and Dorze beehive bamboo village immersion
Ancient origin wild coffee walk in the lush Kaffa rainforests of Jimma & Bonga
included: Private 4WD Land Cruiser throughout with experienced professional expedition driver
Dedicated senior Yared tour director plus local regional specialist guides
11 nights accommodation in premier hand-picked eco-lodges and heritage hotels
All meals (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner) and continuous purified bottled water

Internal domestic transport and airport transfers

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa Cultural Kickoff
itinerary.description: Meet your expedition director for an orientation. Visit the National Museum and Holy Trinity Cathedral, ending with a welcome traditional dinner.

itinerary.title: Addis to Eastern Citadel of Harar
itinerary.description: Travel east through the Awash valley to the sacred walled city of Harar. Witness the thrilling nightly wild hyena feeding ceremony.

itinerary.title: Harar Jugol Walled City Exploration
itinerary.description: Explore the maze-like streets of Harar Jugol, Rimbaud House, traditional Harari mansions, and vibrant spice and coffee souks.

itinerary.title: Harar to Bale Mountains National Park
itinerary.description: Scenic overland transition towards the southeastern highlands and Bale Mountains. Afternoon woodland walk at Dinsho among Mountain Nyala.

itinerary.title: Sanetti Afro-Alpine Plateau & Wolf Tracking
itinerary.description: Ascend to 4,000m across the Sanetti Plateau to spot the rare Ethiopian Wolf. Explore the primordial giant lobelias and the mossy Harenna Forest.

itinerary.title: Bale to Lake Hawassa & Rift Valley
itinerary.description: Drive down into the Great Rift Valley to Lake Hawassa. Stroll the lakeside promenade and observe playful colobus monkeys in the canopy.

itinerary.title: Hawassa Fish Market to Arba Minch
itinerary.description: Visit the lively morning fish market on Lake Hawassa. Drive south to Arba Minch with panoramic views across Lake Abaya and Lake Chamo.

itinerary.title: Lake Chamo Crocodile Safari & Dorze Village
itinerary.description: Boat safari among giant crocodiles and hippos on Lake Chamo. Ascend into the Gamo highlands to experience Dorze bamboo architecture and weaving.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch to Jimma Coffee Heartland
itinerary.description: Travel northwest across scenic green valleys to Jimma, historic capital of the western coffee trade. Visit King Abba Jifar’s Palace.

itinerary.title: Jimma to Bonga Wild Coffee Forests
itinerary.description: Deep dive into the Kaffa UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Walk among ancient wild coffee trees and taste pure tree-hive forest honey.

itinerary.title: Wushwush Tea & Coffee Cupping Session
itinerary.description: Visit the Wushwush tea plantations and enjoy an authentic single-origin coffee cupping session with local cooperative producers.

itinerary.title: Return to Addis Ababa & Farewell Celebration
itinerary.description: Return to Addis Ababa for souvenir shopping, final farewell coffee ceremony, and an unforgettable celebration dinner.

title: Historic North – Bahir Dar, Gondar, Lalibela & Axum
tagline: Follow the ancient trail of faith, kings, and culture through Ethiopia’s timeless north.
overview: Step into the cradle of Ethiopian civilization. Cruise Lake Tana to medieval island monasteries housing centuries-old illuminated manuscripts, stand before the thunderous Blue Nile Falls, explore the stone castles of Emperor Fasilides in Gondar ('the Camelot of Africa'), and marvel at Lalibela's eleven monolithic churches hand-carved out of solid volcanic rock—acclaimed as the eighth wonder of the world.
communityImpactFocus: Empowering licensed local community church historians and preserving sacred UNESCO historical architecture.
highlights: All 11 monolithic rock-hewn churches of Lalibela including iconic Bet Giyorgis (St. George)
Private boat cruise on Lake Tana to 14th-century Zege Peninsula painted monasteries
Majestic Royal Enclosure (Fasil Ghebbi) castles in Gondar
Breathtaking Debre Berhan Selassie Church with ceiling of winged angels
Excursion to the thunderous Blue Nile Falls (Tis Isat)
Ancient Axum obelisks and Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion
included: All domestic flights (Addis - Bahir Dar - Gondar - Lalibela - Addis)
Private air-conditioned minibus/coaster transport with professional drivers
Licensed senior historical tour guide throughout + specialized local clerical scholars
7 nights accommodation in carefully selected top heritage hotels & lodges
Full board (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner) and daily purified mineral water
Private chartered boat on Lake Tana
All church entrance permissions, UNESCO heritage fees, and monastery boat dues
notIncluded: Tips for local guides and drivers

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa to Bahir Dar & Lake Tana Monasteries
itinerary.description: Fly to Bahir Dar. Board a private boat on Lake Tana, source of the Blue Nile. Visit the peaceful Zege Peninsula and the famous 14th-century monastery of Ura Kidane Mehret, adorned with vivid biblical frescoes.
itinerary.overnight: Bahir Dar (Kuriftu Resort or Avanti Blue Nile)

itinerary.title: Blue Nile Falls (Tis Isat) & Drive to Gondar
itinerary.description: Morning drive to the magnificent Blue Nile Falls (Tis Isat, 'Water that Smokes'). Walk across an ancient Portuguese stone bridge. In the afternoon, enjoy a picturesque 3-hour drive to the royal city of Gondar.
itinerary.overnight: Gondar (Gondar Hills Resort or Goha Hotel)

itinerary.title: Castles of Gondar & Debre Berhan Selassie
itinerary.description: Explore the UNESCO-inscribed Royal Enclosure (Fasil Ghebbi), featuring medieval stone castles built by Emperor Fasilides. Visit the peaceful Fasilides’ Bath and the enchanting Debre Berhan Selassie Church with its world-famous ceiling of winged Ethiopian angels.
highlights: Debre Berhan Selassie Ceiling of Angels

itinerary.title: Flight to Sacred Lalibela & Northern Church Group
itinerary.description: Fly over rugged mountain peaks to holy Lalibela. In the afternoon, explore the First Group of rock-hewn churches, including the colossal Bet Medhane Alem and the delicately carved Bet Maryam with its ancient bas-reliefs.
highlights: Bet Medhane Alem (World's largest monolithic church)

itinerary.title: Eastern Church Group & The Icon: Bet Giyorgis (St. George)
itinerary.description: Tour the Eastern Group of rock churches, linked by subterranean tunnels and deep trenches. In the afternoon, visit the masterwork of Lalibela: the freestanding, cross-shaped monolithic church of Bet Giyorgis (St. George), carved 12 meters down into pink volcanic tuff.

itinerary.title: Asheton Maryam Mountain Monastery or Yemrehanna Kristos
itinerary.description: Take a mule ride or scenic 4WD drive up Mount Abuna Yosef to Asheton Maryam monastery (3,150m) with sweeping views, or visit Yemrehanna Kristos, a marble and wood church built inside a natural basalt cave predating Lalibela by 80 years.

itinerary.title: Flight to Axum – Ancient Empire & Ark of the Covenant
itinerary.description: Fly to Axum, the earliest capital of the Axumite Empire. Marvel at the giant monolithic granite obelisks, the Queen of Sheba’s Bath, and the Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion, where the sacred biblical Ark of the Covenant is believed to be preserved.
highlights: Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion

itinerary.title: Axum Antiquities & Return to Addis Ababa
itinerary.description: Visit the King Ezana trilingual stone inscription and ancient royal burial tombs. Transfer to Axum Airport for your return flight to Addis Ababa, ready for your international connection.

title: Simien Mountains National Park – Roof of Africa Trekking
tagline: Walk on the roof of Africa – where eagles soar, cliffs fall away, and Gelada baboons watch the sunrise with you.
overview: The Simien Mountains National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site known as 'the Chess Pieces of the Gods' due to its dramatic volcanic pinnacles, deep canyons, and sheer 1,000-meter drop-offs. Hike along spectacular escarpments walking directly alongside peaceful grass-eating Gelada baboon troops, spot rare Walia ibex clambering on sheer basalt cliffs, and marvel at the thunderous Jinbar Waterfall plunging into the abyss.
communityImpactFocus: Employment of certified park scouts, local mule handlers, camp cooks, and supporting high-altitude village conservation.
highlights: Close, gentle encounters with wild endemic Gelada baboon troops grazing on cliffs
Standing at the edge of the 500-meter Jinbar Waterfall abyss
Panoramic views across jagged peaks reaching over 4,000 meters
Spotting the rare Walia ibex and soaring bearded vultures (Lammergeier)
Luxury comfort at Simien Lodge (Africa's highest lodge) or wilderness camping
included: Private 4WD Land Cruiser transport from/to Gondar
Licensed Simien National Park trekking guide and mandatory armed scout
Mule team and handlers for luggage transport
3 nights lodging (Simien Lodge or equipped mountain tented camp)
All meals prepared fresh by mountain camp chef
All park admission tickets, vehicle fees, and community scout dues
High-altitude first aid and emergency response equipment
notIncluded: Personal trekking boots and cold-weather clothing

itinerary.title: Gondar to Debark & Sankaber Camp
itinerary.description: Drive from Gondar to Debark, national park headquarters. Register with park authorities and meet your mountain guide and scout. Drive into the park and embark on a 2-3 hour scenic acclimation trek along the escarpment rim to Sankaber. Watch hundreds of Gelada baboons socializing peacefully on the grassy clifftops.

itinerary.title: Sankaber to Jinbar Waterfall & Geech Camp
itinerary.description: Trek through giant heather forests and across the Jinbar River ridge. Stand in awe at the viewpoint above Jinbar Waterfall, where a mountain stream plummets more than 500 meters into a sheer gorge. Ascend to Geech camp located on a vast windswept plateau.

itinerary.title: Imet Gogo Pinnacle Viewpoint & Chennek
itinerary.description: Early morning hike to Imet Gogo (3,926m), widely recognized as the single most spectacular viewpoint in all of Africa, providing a 360-degree panorama of jagged volcanic monoliths. Continue across high ridges towards Chennek camp, keeping eyes peeled for Walia ibex leaping along the precipice.

itinerary.title: Chennek Sunrise & Return to Gondar
itinerary.description: Catch the majestic sunrise over the high peaks. Take a final morning hike around the crags of Bwahit pass before boarding our 4WD vehicles for the scenic return drive to Gondar.
